race_context: Kokomo School Corporation serves Kokomo and is Howard County's largest school district; Wikipedia lists Dr. Mike Sargent as superintendent {wiki_ksc}. The Kokomo Lantern reported in October 2024 that the district has about 5,400 students and 800 staff {lantern_referendum}. This guide could not open the district's website to confirm current enrollment or the superintendent in 2026.

The board is chosen in staggered elections: three at-large seats were on the 2022 ballot {tribune_2022_results}, and four other members' terms expired in 2024 {tribune_2024_races}. In May 2025 the board appointed Joey Hurlocker to fill the term of the late Charley Hinkle through 2028 {tribune_hurlocker}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the Howard County election office lists the race as 'Kokomo School Corporation - At Large (3 Seats)', so voters choose up to three, not one as shown on the state list {howard_2026}{in_list}. The three at-large seats are held by Lisa Ellison, Nicole Fain Mundy and Issac White, who won them in November 2022 {tribune_2022_results}. Mundy and White are on the ballot; Ellison is listed by the state as a write-in candidate {howard_2026}{in_list}. With two names on the ballot for three seats, all three incumbents are seeking another term.

Board leadership: Ellison was board president in May 2025 {tribune_hurlocker}. Search-result text indicates the board named Mundy president and White vice president for 2026, but this guide could not open that article.

Budget and property taxes (2024–2026): voters rejected the district's first operating referendum in November 2024, which would have raised about $6.1 million a year for staff pay, academic support and technology {lantern_referendum}{ipm_referendum_result}. At a Sept. 2, 2026 work session, the board reviewed a proposed 2027 budget with an education fund of more than $48 million and an operations fund of about $18.8 million, and discussed the effect of the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1; a public hearing was set for Oct. 7 and adoption for Oct. 28 {govly_budget}.

Teacher discussion policy (2023): in December 2023 the board unanimously adopted a policy requiring that discipline, class size, teaching methods and curriculum materials be discussed with the Kokomo Teachers Association after a 2023 state law made such discussion optional {tribune_discussion}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for this race.
